title: This chart shows Apple's new iPhones didn't wow consumers and that may hurt the stock
text: This chart shows Apple's new iPhones didn't wow consumers and that may hurt the stock Thomas Franck Reblog A data firm that specializes in tracking social media posts found that the number of people who intend to buy the new Apple products was the lowest measured since 2015. "It's not a good sign for Apple. The last time purchase intent was this low for a Keynote event, Apple sales fell year-over-year for the first time in 13 years," LikeFolio founder Andy Swan wrote Thursday. The reaction to the unveiling of a new generation of iPhones this week was "lackluster" compared with prior new smartphone announcements, which could bode poorly for Apple AAPL 's stock, according to a data firm that tracks social media sentiment and market behavior. The tracking of thousands of social media posts pointed to a marked decline in the number of people interested in buying the new technology, according to LikeFolio founder Andy Swan. Apple unveiled the iPhone XR, the iPhone XS and iPhone XS Max on Wednesday. It also announced a new watch, the Series 4, with improved fitness tracking and new health features. LikeFolio found that the number of people who intend to buy the new Apple products following the presentation was the lowest measured since 2015. "Frankly, it's not a good sign for Apple. The last time purchase intent was this low for a Keynote event, Apple sales fell year-over-year for the first time in 13 years," Swan wrote Thursday. A quick glance at LikeFolio's data show that purchase intent mentions after a keynote appear to be a reliable predictor of Apple's stock movement over the nine subsequent months. tweet For example, the shares gained ground in the nine months after Apple's 2017 event, when social media intent-to-purchase mentions soared for the iPhone 8 and X. In a similar way, in the nine months after the Sept. 9, 2015, media event— when Apple revealed the iPhone 6s and the iPad Pro — its stock dropped 9.5 percent against the S&P 500's 9 percent climb. tweet "Two hours and four products later, the end result was a lower level of purchase intent mentions for Apple products/services than we had seen in either of the two prior years," he added. Swan did note, though, that the Apple Watch Series 4 was the "clear fan favorite," boasting new FDA-approved heart-monitoring features. The upgrades pose a major threat to Fitbit FIT , he added, which plummeted after the reveal; the company's stock is down nearly 7 percent this week. And to be sure, Apple shares have been on a tear in 2018. Its stock is up more than 7 percent in the past month alone, adding to a 33 percent gain so far this year. Despite the price gains, Apple is still relatively cheap based on its current performance. Apple's share price, at $226.41 as of Thursday's close, trades at about 17 times analysts' forecasts for 2019 earnings and 15 times expected 2020 earnings, according to FactSet. That's well below the multiples of other "FAANG" stocks like Amazon AMZN , Netflix NFLX and Facebook FB . Netflix is trading at 84 times projected 2019 earnings, while Amazon is trading at 78 times 2019 results. WATCH: Kovach on latest Apple devices More From CNBC
